resources.string: Use our file format and an AI you choose to convert your export. Review it before adding anything.

Jvy does not send your data to an AI. The copied guide contains only instructions, a fictional example and the schema. Remove personal identifiers before sharing an export with any provider. Never share a PIN, recovery code or bank login.
The guide explains the file format, transfers, dates and currencies. Your AI must ask about anything unclear, not guess.
Copied. No wallet data was included.

Paste the guide into your chosen AI and provide an export you are comfortable sharing. Ask for jvy-import.json and a separate reconciliation report. Supported data includes accounts, transactions, budgets, goals, reservations, planned payments, loans, tags and net-worth items. App settings and credentials are not imported.

Save the JSON file, not a chat transcript or ZIP. Select it below for a read-only validation and count preview. Jvy cannot verify that an AI understood your original export; compare its report and balances yourself.
Choose converted JSON · up to 8 MB

Validation passed, but this is not proof of financial accuracy. Import adds data to this wallet; it does not replace it. Matching account/category names may be reused. Unchanged IDs may be reimported; conflicting records are rejected. New IDs can create duplicates.

Budgets and goal targets use your Jvy base currency; reserve only from accounts in that currency. Loans use their linked account’s currency, or the base currency if unlinked. Check these against the conversion report and back up your wallet first.

Next, choose the base currency used for budgets, goal targets, reservations and unlinked loans in the conversion report. Linked loans use their account’s currency. Account currencies are stored separately.
I checked the conversion report, currencies and counts, and backed up any existing wallet data.
